signature: SUBROUTINE DLASSQ( N, X, INCX, SCALE, SUMSQ )

params.name: n
params.reference: The number of elements to be used from the vector x.

params.name: x
params.reference:
The vector for which a scaled sum of squares is computed.

$$
x( i ) = X( 1 + ( i - 1 ) \, \mathrm{INCX} ), 1 \le i \le n
$$

params.name: incx
params.reference: The increment between successive values of the vector x. If $\mathrm{INCX} > 0$, $X(1+(i-1) \, \mathrm{INCX}) = x(i)$ for $1 \le i \le n$ If $\mathrm{INCX} < 0$, $X(1-(n-i) \, \mathrm{INCX}) = x(i)$ for $1 \le i \le n$ If `INCX = 0`, x isn't a vector so there is no need to call this subroutine. If you call it anyway, it will count x(1) in the vector norm N times.

params.name: scale
params.reference: On entry, the value scale in the equation above. On exit, `SCALE` is overwritten by scale\_out, the scaling factor for the sum of squares.

params.name: sumsq
params.reference: On entry, the value sumsq in the equation above. On exit, `SUMSQ` is overwritten by sumsq\_out, the basic sum of squares from which scale\_out has been factored out.
